resources.string: Off by default: stay on the Radio page, keeping your search and expanded group while audio plays. On: open Playing after selecting a station or source. You can always open Playing yourself.

Off hides radio and stops reception, returning to the saved music queue paused. Stations, pins and cached logos are kept. Radio loads on demand even when enabled; ordinary music startup does not fetch radio data.
Radio is disabled. Enable it under Settings > Radio to listen.

The bundled catalog includes national, provincial and selected international stations. Up to 10 channels can be pinned as shortcuts; eight are pinned initially. Pinned stations also stay in their normal groups with a configurable color. Groups start collapsed. Tap a group or press remote OK to open it; opening another closes the first. Changing search closes groups. Expanded channels use two columns on wide screens, one on narrow screens or with larger fonts. Hold a channel, or focus it and press remote Menu, to pin/unpin, edit addresses or choose a source. Playing shows pinned shortcuts in the lyrics area. National names and region headings follow English/Chinese; supplied station names and groups are retained.

Radio settings contains import/export, reset, return to music, pin color, buffering, retries, source fallback, logos and live status. M3U groups take precedence; otherwise names identify regions, with unknown names in Others.

Export M3U saves the complete current list for offline editing. Import always asks whether to keep and merge or replace all current stations. Merge skips identical sources and adds different URLs to matching stations. Replace all keeps only valid file entries, including after restart; unlisted built-ins stay removed until Reset built-ins. Pins survive only for retained IDs. Keep exported IDs when renaming. Reset restores the whole bundled catalog while keeping additional user-created channels and remaining pins. Imports never edit the source file or delete music.

Audio uses the Internet, not an FM tuner. Stop disconnects; Play rejoins live audio. Rewind/forward selects the previous/next source of the SAME station without wrapping; unavailable directions are disabled. Local music keeps its 10-second seek controls. Radio has no recording or timeline seeking. Automatic source fallback is optional and bounded.

No logos are bundled. Only the playing station downloads its configured logo, at most 512 KiB, resized to at most 128 pixels. Disk copies remain until cleared. Browsing, import/export and startup never fetch streams or logos. Marks belong to their broadcasters and imply no endorsement.

Actual list changes stop radio, not local music. Export does not interrupt playback. The catalog loads off the main thread only when needed. Disabling Radio returns to the saved music queue paused; enabling never autoplays. Availability depends on the broadcaster and network. Some supplied URLs are old or unencrypted; TDM Macau links may be unreachable outside supported networks.

Save the complete radio list to local storage or USB for offline editing, not just the search results or pinned stations. The UTF-8 M3U contains names, stable IDs, groups, logo URLs and every playing source; no audio or images are downloaded. Keep a station’s ID when renaming it. Import the edited file to merge it or replace the entire list.
Radio list exported: %1$d stations, %2$d playing sources. Edit the UTF-8 M3U and import it when ready.
There are no stations to export. Import a list or reset the built-ins first.
The complete export exceeds the import limit of 1 MiB or 5,000 source entries. No partial list was written. A local ZIP backup can preserve the full catalog.

Restore the names, groups, logos and addresses of ALL bundled stations, including regional and international channels? Edits to those stations will be reset. Additional user-created channels and pins are kept. Radio reception stops; local music and its queue are unchanged.
The complete bundled catalog was restored. Additional channels and pins were kept.

Save as UTF-8 TXT/M3U/M3U8, up to 1 MiB, 5,000 source entries and 32 sources per station. Export M3U writes the complete current list in this format, without downloading audio or logos.

TXT: name,URL per line; commas inside the URL are preserved. Stable IDs use three tab-separated columns: ID, name, URL. A line Province,#genre# sets the group for following TXT channels.

M3U:
#EXTM3U
#EXTINF:-1 tvg-id="radio:cnr:zgzs" group-title="National",Voice of China
https://ngcdn001.cnr.cn/live/zgzs/index.m3u8

Optional tvg-logo="https://…/logo.png" is downloaded only during playback. #EXTGRP groups are supported. Repeat the same ID/name for each different source URL. Export repeats its metadata for each source; edit all entries of that station consistently. The last entry supplies the name and supplied group/logo. Empty group-title or tvg-logo restores automatic grouping or the built-in logo. Backslash-escape quotes and backslashes inside quoted attributes.

Import always asks: Keep and merge retains current stations/addresses, skips identical sources, and adds different sources to matching names. Replace all stations keeps only valid file entries, removing unlisted stations and old sources, including built-ins. Cancel changes nothing. Reset built-ins restores the bundled catalog.

Keep exported IDs when renaming. Known existing IDs take precedence; otherwise known URLs/names or normalized names match stations, even when a new list supplies a different provider ID. Use direct HTTP/HTTPS audio or HLS URLs, not web pages, local paths, nested playlists or HLS manifests. Custom headers are ignored. Only import trusted lists; HTTP audio and logos are unencrypted. Old URLs may not work.
